title: Rosemary Potato Rolls
changes_from_base: Egg-free olive oil dough with potato flakes, milk powder and rosemary, cut into flour-dusted triangles.
summary: Light, egg-free olive oil rolls with rosemary and a soft crumb from potato flakes, cut into flour-dusted triangles.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel
baking tray lined with baking paper

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the water, oil and yeast together in a large bowl. Whisk the milk powder and potato flakes into the flour, then add this with the sugar, rosemary and salt and mix to a soft dough.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead 6 min on low speed or 8 min by hand, until satiny and springy. If it feels stiff after a few minutes, work in another 1-2 tbsp water.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave about 1 h, until almost doubled.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Press the dough down and roll it into a log about 55 cm long. Mist or brush the top with water, dust with flour, then cut it into 16 triangles with a base of about 5 cm, alternating the angle of the knife. Space them out on the tray.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover and leave about 45 min, until puffy. Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan).

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15-18 min, until pale golden on top and browned underneath; the centre reads about 93 °C. Cool on a rack.

tips: Chop the rosemary very finely so it does not tear the dough.
Alternate the angle of the knife to get triangles with no waste.
Bake on a hot tray for a crisper base.
storage: Keep cooled rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 180 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
